The challenge can still support its conclusions -- every erratum was re-derived independently and none reverses a safety finding -- but a 12.5% truth-defect rate is high and is the main thing a v3 should fix.

overall_reasoning: Every structural requirement holds: the freeze provably predates the run, the truth was never edited, the first run is immutable, the no-peek audit is clean and has been shown able to fail, no forbidden corpus was opened, and the certified Core was byte-identical when the run started. Two concerns are recorded and neither is disqualifying: a 12.5% truth-defect rate, and discovery contamination on six errata whose repairs were nonetheless independent. The challenge's conclusions -- two false accepts from one contract defect, zero Core crashes, zero unjustified metamorphic violations -- rest on evidence that survives its own errata.
question: Is this blind challenge itself valid, independently of how the Core scored?
